question: A 67-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of generalized fatigue. On examination, he appears pale. He also has multiple pinpoint, red, nonblanching spots on his extremities. His spleen is significantly enlarged. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 8.3 g/dL, a leukocyte count of 81,000/mm3, and a platelet count of 35,600/mm3. A peripheral blood smear shows immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Generalized fatigue" -> "Pallor" -> "Pinpoint, red, nonblanching spots on extremities" -> "Significantly enlarged spleen" -> "Hemoglobin concentration of 8.3 g/dL" -> "Leukocyte count of 81,000/mm3" -> "Platelet count of 35,600/mm3" -> "Immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and cytoplasmic inclusions on peripheral blood smear" -> "Most likely diagnosis: Acute myelogenous leukemia" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Generalized fatigue" -> "Pallor" -> "Pinpoint, red, nonblanching spots on extremities" -> "Significantly enlarged spleen" -> "Hemoglobin concentration of 8.3 g/dL" -> "Leukocyte count of 81,000/mm3" -> "Platelet count of 35,600/mm3" -> "Immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and cytoplasmic inclusions on peripheral blood smear" -> "Possible diagnosis: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia" -> 80%
analysis: The presentation of generalized fatigue, pale appearance, splenomegaly, low hemoglobin, low platelet count, and presence of immature cells with Auer rods on peripheral blood smear are indicative of acute myelogenous leukemia (AML). The presence of Auer rods is a characteristic feature of AML.
